critical_code_review_comments: server.py GET /api/content: seed is inserted with `dict(APP_CONTENT_SEED)` (shallow copy) — motor mutates the doc adding `_id`; the returned `doc` is then rebuilt as `{k: v for k, v in APP_CONTENT_SEED.items()}` on the first-request branch which strips `_id`, and the second-request branch uses `find_one(..., {'_id': 0})` which also strips it. Both branches confirmed clean (verified: no `_id` in JSON). Still, using `dict(APP_CONTENT_SEED)` for insert only shallow-copies nested lists/dicts, so an accidental mutation on the seed elsewhere would leak into APP_CONTENT_SEED. Consider `copy.deepcopy(APP_CONTENT_SEED)` for safety.

server.py mounts `/api/assets` StaticFiles AFTER `app.include_router(api_router)` and adds CORS middleware AFTER the router include — order works because FastAPI mounts are effective independently, but conventionally middleware should be added before include_router. Non-blocking.
src/lib/remoteContent.ts stores the whole content JSON under CACHE_KEY on every successful fetch — fine for size (< 30KB), but consider a lightweight ETag/If-Modified-Since when the content grows.

VerbaleSection.tsx calls loadAppContent() on mount independently of the parent risultati screen which likely does the same via importi/faq — 2 to 3 GETs happen per session. Cache dedup at loadAppContent (in-memory promise) would prevent parallel refetches (minor perf).
